newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan banks need "sense of crisis" on reform-panel.
newsitem.headline: Japan banks need "sense of crisis" on reform-panel.

text.p: Japanese banks should deal aggressively with financial system reforms, with a "sense of crisis", the chairman of the Financial System Research Council, an advisory body to Japan's Finance Ministry, told reporters on Friday.
He said that it is necessary to impose strict penalties in order to prevent scandals involving financial institutions.

"The key to making the reforms successful will be whether financial institutions deal with (them) with a sense of crisis. I would like financial institutions to look seriously at the current situation," said Ryuichiro Tachi, the council's chairman.
He added, "What I really feel sorry about is that there is a scandal which is beyond my comprehension. On that point, (regulators) should deal strictly with any violation of the rules."
The council earlier on Friday announced a series of sweeping reform proposals for Japan's banking sector.
